instructions.question: What overall sentiment does the tweet's author express — positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Judge the author's own feeling, not the topic: excitement, anticipation, praise, wishes, congratulations or invitations framed enthusiastically are positive; complaints, insults, anger, sadness, disappointment or sarcastic jabs are negative. Plain news, schedules, questions, customer-service replies and invitations without emotional framing are neutral, as are mild opinions or jokes whose tone is unclear or mixed. Sarcastic praise usually counts as positive only if the surface wording is upbeat and the target isn't clearly attacked.

neutral.what: Factual news, scores, schedules, job ads, plain questions, service replies, or opinions/jokes with no clear emotional stance.
examples: American Dustin Johnson leads the PGA Championship after the 1st round at Whistling Straits on 6 under par.
Who going with me to Knott's Saturday?
@user Hey Milan - A member of our team has sent you an email. Please reply there with any questions you may have.
I'm not sure what Rahul Gandhi is trying to accomplish with all of this
neutral.cues: headlines, scores, dates, 'who is going', 'check out', retweeted news, informational tone
neutral.not_for: News framed with excitement or praise is positive; reported facts with an author's complaint or insult are negative.

positive.what: Author expresses happiness, excitement, anticipation, praise, love, gratitude, good wishes, or promotes something enthusiastically.
examples: Woot!  So excited that I get to watch tonight's game. Go Colts!!
I want IHOP tomorrow morning
Jurassic World is back in @user theaters for one week starting Friday! Who's going?!
Congratulations to Olivia Jordan, who won Miss USA on Sunday!!
positive.cues: Happy, excited, can't wait, love, best, bless, good luck, congratulations, Go [team]!, :), hype, Looking forward
positive.not_for: Bare event announcements or 'who's going with me?' questions without enthusiasm are neutral; tweets with 'happy' used ironically are negative.

negative.what: Author expresses anger, frustration, sadness, disappointment, contempt, insults, or hostile political criticism, including sarcastic put-downs.
examples: The Knicks vs Nets game got moved all the way to the 26th damn
@user BY HAVING Seth Rollins as number 1? All credibility is lost. May be the worst WWE champion in history!
One of my favorite characters on Game Of Thrones just died I can't go to school tomorrow I'm grieving
SimCity delayed it’s availability
negative.cues: wtf, damn, fuck, sucks, worst, idiot, joke, can't, missed, sad, crying, cringe, delayed, punish
negative.not_for: Strong words used in excitement ('kick ass', 'fuckin' blessed') are positive; dramatic jokes with no real complaint can be neutral.
